summary: The Fed's hawkish pivot — Warsh's first meeting projections leaning toward tightening, a sharp reversal from March's rate-cut path — has been the week's dominant force, lifting short-term yields and pressuring risk assets. Gold is on track for a third consecutive weekly decline, hit by a stronger dollar at a one-year high and rising odds of a Fed rate hike, with markets pricing roughly a 70% probability of an increase by September.
tweet: A dollar at one-year highs and a hawkish Fed tilt are driving gold's third straight weekly loss while stocks claw back from last week's FOMC sell-off.
